points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the captured record.

A real Chrome session read the complete first two US-English pages without CAPTCHA. Page one contains the bucket restore guide and overview, a 2024 blog, Server Fault, object restore docs, disaster recovery material and old project-deletion questions; page two continues with forums, object-focused tutorials, the JSON restore method, Go package docs and a generic project-restore video.

G2=pass: the SERP is fragmented across documentation inner pages, forums, API reference, object-only instructions and generic project recovery. It has no exact-task media or strong-brand takeover and shows a composite-task quality cliff.

Google's live bucket guide, updated 2026-08-12 UTC, completely explains listing and restoring a soft-deleted bucket, generation numbers, name collisions, IAM, console/gcloud/API paths and subsequent object restoration. However, it assumes the project context is available and does not explain deleted-project recovery.

G3=pass: no result completes the combined sequence of recovering a deleted project and then listing/restoring its soft-deleted bucket. The JSON API reference is a component of the same official path, while object tutorials and old project questions do not provide the composite workflow.
This is not veto_window_bet because no second already-built exact composite implementation is merely awaiting indexing.
Window estimate is weeks, expiring 2026-09-20. Bucket soft-delete restoration is newly documented, but mature component docs and forum demand can produce an exact combined guide quickly.

Invalidation conditions: two free end-to-end deleted-project plus soft-deleted-bucket recovery guides enter the SERP; Google adds the project-deletion scenario to the bucket guide; bucket retention, restore IAM, generation handling, or project recovery behavior changes.
